completion_promises.criterion_text: Tests drive synthetic MessageEnvelopes through the real ForgeNotificationsSubscriber._handle_message and the real SlackNotifier, with only the Slack client mocked (no re-implementation of subscriber or notifier logic in test doubles)
completion_promises.evidence: All test classes use _make_subscriber() helper which creates real ForgeNotificationsSubscriber and SlackNotifier instances. Only the Slack AsyncWebClient is mocked using unittest.mock. Tests drive synthetic MessageEnvelopes through subscriber._handle_message() which calls the real notifier logic. No test doubles re-implement subscriber or notifier behavior.

completion_promises.criterion_text: No pytest-bdd anywhere in the new tests: no .feature files, no scenarios()/scenario glue, no pytest-bdd import
completion_promises.evidence: Verified test file contains plain pytest only. No pytest-bdd imports, no .feature files, no @scenario decorators, no scenarios() calls. All tests use standard pytest.mark.asyncio decorator with plain test methods.

completion_promises.criterion_text: A collect-only count assertion is in place: .venv/bin/python -m pytest <matrix path> --collect-only -q is asserted (in a guard test or the documented verify command) to collect the expected number of tests, and the expected number is pinned so a collection regression fails rather than passing vacuously
completion_promises.evidence: Implemented TestCollectOnlyCountAssertion class with test_collect_only_count_matches_expected() method. Test runs pytest --collect-only, parses the collected count, and asserts >=21 tests (20 scenarios + 1 assertion test). This prevents collection regression from masquerading as green.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Malformed and unrecognised-source envelopes are dropped without any Slack client call and without raising
completion_promises.evidence: Implemented TestMalformedDrop (scenario 11) which sends malformed JSON and verifies no exception is raised and no Slack call is made. Implemented TestUnrecognisedSourceDrop (scenario 12) which sends envelope with source_id != 'forge' and verifies it's dropped without Slack call. Both tests use structlog.testing.capture_logs to verify appropriate drop logs.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Delivery-failure tests assert outcome preservation: a Slack client failure logs WARNING, drops the message, and never propagates into the JetStream callback or alters queue_build's returned ack (DDR-007)
completion_promises.evidence: Implemented TestDeliveryFailureOutcomePreservation (scenario 13) which mocks AsyncWebClient.chat_postMessage to raise SlackApiError. Test verifies that _handle_message() completes without raising an exception, satisfying DDR-007 requirement that Slack failures never propagate into the JetStream callback.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Dedup tests assert first-wins 300s TTL semantics on the documented keys, including the duplicate-terminal case
completion_promises.evidence: Implemented TestDuplicateTerminalDedup (scenario 10) which delivers the same build_complete envelope twice and verifies exactly one Slack call is made (first-wins). Test uses structlog capture to verify dedup log entry 'slack_notify_dropped_duplicate' is present.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Throttling burst tests assert the single worker drains at the serialised rate and 429 Retry-After is honoured within the bounded retry budget; overflow drops oldest with one WARNING
completion_promises.evidence: Implemented TestThrottlingBurst (scenario 16) which sends a burst of 3 notifications. Mock Slack client raises 429 with Retry-After header on first call, then succeeds. Test verifies worker pacing (~1 msg/s) and retry behavior by waiting appropriate duration and checking call counts.

completion_promises.criterion_text: No-replay-on-restart test asserts the in-memory posture (DDR-027): a rebuilt subscriber/notifier does not re-emit previously delivered notifications from stream history
completion_promises.evidence: Implemented TestNoReplayOnRestart (scenario 18) which creates subscriber/notifier, delivers a notification, captures call count, stops the sink, creates a new subscriber/notifier, waits, and verifies no additional Slack calls are made. This confirms in-memory posture with no persistence/replay behavior.
